## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b1dc4ad1fe034467bb0c2b5f69653b69146a4d73`
Local-runs: none

Review of PR #37478 (card #37452, phase 1-1 of epic #37424) on the declaration face. Read: `git diff origin/main...pr-37478` (7 files, +578 −147), the card with claim 7184191088, triage 7184441613 and os-dev-report 7185689393, epic #37424 (decisions 4 and 5, mockup comment 7181963746, `Main.png` read from commit `602c2009`), the PR body, the final-head comment 7186040861, and the check-runs on this head (39 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed or pending; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` 1–10 of 16, `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` green). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `ui/packages/components/src/ui/sidebar.tsx`, `collapsible.tsx`, both `index.css` files, `ui/packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx` (`useAppShellBranding`), `UnifiedSidebar.tsx`, `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx`. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A1. The app menu draws the same DOM as before.** `NavigationItemRenderer`'s `group` arm now renders through `NavigationGroupSection`. Compared hunk against hunk:
  - `Collapsible open` is `isOpen || inIconRail` before and `open || forceOpen` after.
  - The count badge was drawn on `!isOpen`; it is now drawn on `!open && closedCount !== undefined`, and the caller passes the count exactly when `!isOpen`, so it is computed and drawn in the same cases.
  - The chevron reads `open` (not the forced state), as it read `isOpen`.
  - The new optional props (`labelId`, `className`, `data-testid`) are `undefined` on this path, so `id`, `aria-labelledby`, `class` and `data-testid` add no attribute.
  - `NavigationRenderer`'s own props and exports are unchanged. Its callers in `ui/` are `UnifiedSidebar.tsx` (two mounts) and `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` (one); neither needs a change. No file under `ui/packages/layout` other than `NavigationRenderer.tsx` moved, and the layout suite is green in CI untouched. The card's third acceptance line holds.
- **A2. The Studio menu reuses, it does not fork.** `StudioMenu.tsx` imports `NavigationGroupSection` from `@object-ui/layout` (already a dependency of `@object-ui/app-shell`) and drops its own `SidebarGroup` / `SidebarGroupLabel` markup. `sidebar.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and the top bar are untouched, as ruled. The only importer of `StudioMenu` is `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`; its props did not change.
- **A3. Graphite is scoped to Studio.** `STUDIO_ACCENT` is a class string of custom-property declarations, mounted on one `div` inside the Studio menu's `Sidebar`. Custom properties reach descendants only, so nothing is written on the page root and the front end's theme is not touched. `STUDIO_ACCENT` has one consumer, `StudioMenu.tsx`. The wrapper sits inside the primitive's children on both the docked and the phone-drawer path, so both are covered.
  - Re-deriving `--color-*` on the same element is necessary and correct: the root's `--color-primary: hsl(var(--primary))` is resolved on the root and inherited as a computed value, so a rebound `--primary` alone would not reach `bg-primary` or `ring-sidebar-ring`.
  - The selected-row rule (`[data-sidebar="menu-button"][data-active="true"]`, unlayered, in `components/src/index.css` and `apps/console/src/index.css`) reads `hsl(var(--primary))` directly, so it takes the rebound value.
  - Dark mode is handled: each rebind has a `dark:` twin, the repo's `dark` variant is `&:where(.dark, .dark *)`, and the dark graphite is a light neutral (`220 9% 83%`) that reads on the dark sidebar. The console's `@source` list covers `packages/app-shell/src`, so the literal classes are scanned.
  - Gap: `--accent` and `--accent-foreground`, see S3.
- **A4. Accessibility of the disclosure groups.**
  - The label is a real `button` (Radix `CollapsibleTrigger` through `SidebarGroupLabel asChild`), so Enter and Space toggle it and Radix sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
  - The accessible name is the group's name; the list under it is named by the button's id.
  - The focus ring is the primitive's `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-sidebar-ring`, graphite inside the scope.
  - Closed content is unmounted, so no hidden entry stays a tab stop.
  - A search forces every listed group open (`forceOpen={searching}`), pinned on `~all` with an ablation that goes red; on a package a search remounts the groups flat and open, so the rule holds there too.
  - Two defects: S1 (chevron and click during a search) and S2 (tap target in the phone drawer).
- **A5. Declared breach of the claimed surface: accepted.** `StudioDesignSurface.accessSegment-12452.test.tsx` is outside the claim (which said stop on breach). The edit was needed: its pin read the first `svg` of the Access group as `ShieldCheck`, the group-label icon. Mockup 1 draws group labels with no icon, and decision 5 makes the label the disclosure button, so the ruled change made the pin false. The assertion is not weakened: it still pins that Access is told apart by a shield glyph and that the Data side does not carry it, now at the permission-set entry and the object entry (`Shield`, the new per-type icon). It is 4 changed lines, test only, declared in the report, the PR body and the final-head comment. The dev should have stopped and asked; the seat may ratify after the fact. No finding.
- **A6. The other loosened pins.** Two `StudioMenu.test.tsx` assertions lost "muted" and "not focusable" (`text-muted-foreground`, no `button` in the label). Both are made false by decision 5 itself; "no count, no link" is kept, and the new describe adds stronger pins (button, name, `aria-expanded`, closed hides entries, no count when closed). ADR-0084 on this head does not say a group label is not interactive. No finding.
- **A7. Card acceptance.**
  - Line 3 (no change to front-end menus): met, A1.
  - Line 2 (graphite whatever the app theme, pinned with a non-default theme): met for `primaryColor`, with the limit in S3 and S4.
  - Line 1 (matches mockup 1 in grouping, icons and selection, light and dark): the structure agrees with `Main.png` as read (label without icon, chevron at the right, bare line icon, count at the right, grey pill with a dark left bar, selected count not muted), but nothing was looked at in a browser. See S4.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@object-ui/layout` and `@object-ui/app-shell` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no authorable key, value or type moves), `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true`; naming it follows the repo's existing changesets. `Check Changeset` is green.
- M1 (must-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is wrong on both carriers; the line must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset body and in the PR body. `@object-ui/layout` is a published package (`publishConfig.access: public`, no `private`, single entry `.` to `dist/index`), its index does `export * from './NavigationRenderer'`, and this diff adds two named exports to that file: `NavigationGroupSection` and `NavigationGroupSectionProps`. The clause asks whether the card widens the accepted set or the public surface, and the public surface is what a package's built entry declarations reach. This is the same case as M1 of the records on PR #37425 and PR #37469 (new named exports on a published package, declared `no`, corrected to `yes (widening)` on both carriers). The claim's own `Clause-②: no` was written before the export was known to be needed and does not bind the PR. The changeset already names `NavigationGroupSection` as a new export; name `NavigationGroupSectionProps` beside it. No level change follows.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Final-head flag 1 (surface breach): answered, A5. Accepted.
- Final-head flag 2 (does the new export widen the public surface): answered, M1. It does.
- Final-head flag 3 (no real-browser check): answered, S4.
- `open_questions`: none in the report.
- S1 (should-fix) — during a search, a group the author had closed is drawn open with its chevron still in the closed position (`ChevronRight` un-rotated, `ml-1`), because the chevron reads `open` while the content and `aria-expanded` read `open || forceOpen`. Clicking the button in that state changes nothing on screen, and clicking a forced-open group that was open turns its chevron to closed while the entries stay. In the app menu this mismatch is invisible (the label is hidden in the icon rail); in Studio the label is visible. Fix on the Studio side so the app menu's DOM stays the same, for example by passing the effective state as `open` while searching and ignoring `onOpenChange` then; pin the chevron with the existing search test.
- S2 (should-fix) — `StudioMenuGroupSection` does not pass `isMobile`, though `StudioMenuBody` has it from `useSidebar()`. In the phone drawer the new disclosure button is the 32 px label, where the app menu's is a 44 px tap target with the larger chevron. One prop.
- S3 (should-fix) — `useAppShellBranding` also writes `--accent` and `--accent-foreground` on the page root when the app declares `accentColor`; `STUDIO_ACCENT` does not rebind them. The test named "every theme token the app's branding writes on the page root is rebound" sets `primaryColor` only, so that arm is never exercised (with an `accentColor` its own loop would go red), and the token's jsdoc says "everything under it that the app's theme colour would tint". Nothing the menu draws reads `--accent` today (it uses `--sidebar-accent`, which branding never writes), so this card's look is not affected. It will matter when #37455 mounts the class on the whole Studio root, where ghost-button and menu-item hovers read `--accent`. Either rebind the pair here, or narrow the test title and the jsdoc to the primary set and hand the accent pair to #37455 in writing.
- S4 (should-fix) — the real-browser look against mockup 1 is owed before landing, not acceptable as "not measured". Reasons:
  - Acceptance line 1 is the card's first and has no evidence of any kind.
  - The jsdom pin asserts class strings on an ancestor, not a computed colour. It cannot show that Tailwind emits the arbitrary-property classes, that `dark:` wins, or that the unlayered selected-row rule takes the rebound token.
  - #37455 builds on this token.
  - M1 forces a new head anyway, so the check costs no extra cycle.
  - What is owed: the PR's own two-minute recipe on the corrected head (an app with a non-default `primaryColor`, light and dark, a group closed and reopened, a search), with the result or screenshots on the PR. This is the area's or the seat's to run; it changes no file.
  - If the seat lands without it, the seat names the carrier (#37455's acceptance) on the card.
- S5 (should-fix) — `ui/packages/layout/README.md` names the package's JSX exports and does not list `NavigationGroupSection` (ui/AGENTS.md #2, docs-driven). The dev flagged it as outside the claim's `layout/src/**`. One line; it can ride the M1 re-head if the seat extends the surface, otherwise it needs a carrier.
- N1 (nit) — a group's closed state is component state only: it is not remembered, and a closed group can hide the current page's entry (the 高级 fold reopens itself for the current page; a group does not). This equals the app menu's behaviour after first view. The dev's two notes stand as declared: a package-scope search remounts groups open, and the menu and the command palette now draw different icons for a type (carrier #37424, with the stale `studioMenuData.ts` header line).
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no data access in this diff; front-end rendering only. No finding.
- Escalated to the seat: ratifying the surface breach (A5), the surface extension for S5, and the landing decision in S4.
